verses.1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Joel, the son of Bethuel.
verses.1:2: Hear these things, you elders, and give ear, all you who dwell in the land. Have such things happened in our days, or in the days of your fathers?
verses.1:3: Tell your children concerning them, and let your children tell their children, and their children to another generation.
verses.1:4: What the caterpillar left, the locust devoured; and what the locust left, the hopping locust devoured; and what the hopping locust left, the blight devoured.
verses.1:5: Awake from their wine, you drunkards, and weep; lament, all you who drink wine to drunkenness, for gladness and joy have been taken away from your mouth.
verses.1:6: For a nation has come up against My land, strong and without number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and its jaw teeth are those of a young lion.
verses.1:7: It has turned My vine to desolation, and My fig trees to splintered ruin; searching, it thoroughly searched it out and cast it down; it has made its branches white.
verses.1:8: Lament to Me more than a bride girded with sackcloth for the husband of her virginity.
verses.1:9: Sacrifice and drink offering have been taken away from the house of the Lord; mourn, you priests who minister at the altar.
verses.1:10: For the plains are laid waste; let the land mourn, for the grain is laid waste, the wine is dried up, the oil has diminished.
verses.1:11: The farmers are dried up; lament, you estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest has perished from the field.
verses.1:12: The vine has dried up, and the fig trees have diminished; pomegranate and palm and apple tree, and all the trees of the field, have dried up, because the sons of men have put joy to shame.
verses.1:13: Gird yourselves and mourn, you priests; lament, you who minister at the altar; go in, sleep in sackcloth, you who minister to God, for sacrifice and drink offering have been withheld from the house of your God.
verses.1:14: Sanctify a fast, proclaim a solemn service, gather the elders, all who dwell in the land, to the house of your God, and cry out earnestly to the Lord:
verses.1:15: "Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the day of the Lord is near, and as devastation from devastation it shall come."
verses.1:16: Before your eyes provisions have been utterly destroyed; from the house of your God, gladness and joy.
verses.1:17: Heifers have leaped at their mangers, storehouses have been laid waste, winepresses have been torn down, because the grain has dried up.
verses.1:18: What shall we lay up for ourselves? The herds of cattle have wept, because there was no pasture for them, and the flocks of sheep have perished.
verses.1:19: To You, O Lord, I will cry out, for fire has consumed the fair places of the wilderness, and flame has set ablaze all the trees of the field.
verses.1:20: Even the beasts of the plain have looked up to You, for the channels of water have dried up, and fire has devoured the fair places of the wilderness.
verses.2:1: Sound the trumpet in Zion, proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who dwell in the land be confounded, for the day of the Lord is present, for it is near.
verses.2:2: A day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick mist! Like the dawn, a great and mighty people shall be poured out upon the mountains; none like it has existed from eternity, nor after it shall there be any again, even to the years of generations of generations.
verses.2:3: Before it is a consuming fire, and behind it a blazing flame; like a paradise of delight is the land before its face, and behind it a plain of desolation, and there shall be no one who escapes it.
verses.2:4: Like the appearance of horses is their appearance, and like horsemen, so shall they pursue.
verses.2:5: Like the sound of chariots they shall leap upon the tops of the mountains, and like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, and like a great and mighty people drawn up in array for battle.
verses.2:6: Before its face peoples shall be crushed; every face is like the scorching of a pot.
verses.2:7: Like warriors they shall run, and like men of war they shall climb upon the walls; each one shall march in his own way, and they shall by no means turn aside from their paths.
verses.2:8: Each one shall not keep away from his brother; weighed down in their armor they shall march, and upon their missiles they shall fall, yet they shall by no means be brought to an end.
verses.2:9: They shall seize the city, and upon the walls they shall run, and upon the houses they shall climb, and through the windows they shall enter like thieves.
verses.2:10: Before its face the earth shall be confounded and the heaven shall be shaken; the sun and the moon shall grow dark, and the stars shall withdraw their brightness.
verses.2:11: And the Lord shall utter His voice before the face of His host, for exceedingly great is His camp, for mighty are the works of His words; for great is the day of the Lord, great and exceedingly manifest, and who shall be sufficient for it?
verses.2:12: And now, says the Lord your God, "Turn back to Me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning."
verses.2:13: And rend your hearts and not your garments, and turn back to the Lord your God, for He is merciful and compassionate, longsuffering and rich in mercy, and He relents over calamities.
verses.2:14: Who knows whether He will turn and relent, and leave behind Him a blessing—a sacrifice and a drink offering for the Lord our God?
verses.2:15: Sound the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, proclaim a solemn service.
verses.2:16: Gather the people, sanctify the assembly, select the elders, gather the infants nursing at the breasts; let the bridegroom go forth from his chamber and the bride from her bridal canopy.
verses.2:17: In the midst of the base of the altar the priests who minister to the Lord shall weep and say, "Spare Your people, O Lord, and do not give Your inheritance to reproach, that the nations should rule over them; lest they say among the nations, 'Where is their God?'"
verses.2:18: And the Lord was zealous for His land, and He spared His people.
verses.2:19: And the Lord answered and said to His people, "Behold, I am sending forth to you the grain and the wine and the oil, and you shall be filled with them; and I will no longer give you over to reproach among the nations.
verses.2:20: And the one from the north I will drive away from you, and I will thrust him out into a waterless land, and I will destroy his face into the first sea and his rear into the last sea; and his putrefaction shall ascend, and his stench shall ascend, because he has magnified his deeds."
verses.2:21: Take courage, O land, rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has done great things.
verses.2:22: Take courage, you beasts of the plain, for the plains of the wilderness have sprouted; for the tree has borne its fruit, and the fig tree and the vine have yielded their strength.
verses.2:23: And you children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, for He has given you provisions for righteousness, and He will rain down for you the early rain and the late rain, just as before.
verses.2:24: And the threshing floors shall be filled with grain, and the vats shall overflow with wine and oil.
verses.2:25: And He will repay you for the years that the locust and the hopping locust and the blight and the caterpillar devoured—My great host, which I sent against you.
verses.2:26: And you shall eat to the full and be satisfied, and you shall praise the name of the Lord your God for the wondrous things He has done with you; and My people shall by no means be put to shame forever.
verses.2:27: And you shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and there is none else besides Me; and My people shall never again be put to shame forever.
verses.3:1: And it shall come to pass after these things that I will pour out of My Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
verses.3:2: And upon My menservants and upon the maidservants in those days I will pour out of My Spirit.
verses.3:3: And I will give wonders in heaven, and upon the earth blood and fire and vapor of smoke.
verses.3:4: The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the coming of the great and manifest day of the Lord.
verses.3:5: And it shall come to pass that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be one who escapes, just as the Lord has spoken, and those receiving good tidings, whom the Lord has called.
verses.4:1: For behold, in those days and at that time, when I Myself restore the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.4:2: I will also gather all the nations and lead them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat; and I will enter into judgment with them there on behalf of My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land,
verses.4:3: and they cast lots for My people; they gave the young boys to harlots, and sold the young girls for wine and drank.
verses.4:4: And what are you to Me, Tyre and Sidon, and all Galilee of the foreigners? Are you repaying a recompense to Me, or do you bear malice against Me hastily? And swiftly I will return your recompense upon your heads,
verses.4:5: because you have taken My silver and My gold, and have brought My choice and fine things into your temples;
verses.4:6: and the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem you have sold to the sons of the Greeks, that you might drive them out from their borders.
verses.4:7: Behold, I will raise them up out of the place where you sold them, and I will return your recompense upon your heads,
verses.4:8: and I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they shall sell them into captivity to a nation far away; for the Lord has spoken.
verses.4:9: Proclaim these things among the nations: Consecrate war, rouse the warriors; draw near and come up, all you men of war.
verses.4:10: Beat your plows into swords and your sickles into spears; let the weak one say, "I have strength."
verses.4:11: Assemble yourselves and come in, all you nations on every side, and be gathered together there; let the meek become a warrior.
verses.4:12: Let them be roused, let all the nations come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the nations on every side.
verses.4:13: Send forth the sickles, for the vintage is at hand; go in, tread, for the winepress is full; cause the vats to overflow, for their evils have been multiplied.
verses.4:14: Sounds have resounded in the valley of judgment, for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of judgment.
verses.4:15: The sun and the moon shall grow dark, and the stars shall withdraw their radiance.
verses.4:16: And the Lord shall cry aloud from Zion, and utter His voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth shall be shaken; yet the Lord shall spare His people and strengthen the sons of Israel.
verses.4:17: And you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who dwells in Zion, on My holy mountain; and Jerusalem shall be holy, and foreigners shall pass through her no more.
verses.4:18: And it shall come to pass in that day that the mountains shall drip sweetness, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the channels of Judah shall flow with waters; and a fountain shall go forth from the house of the Lord and shall water the brook of rushes.
verses.4:19: Egypt shall become a desolation, and Idumea shall become a plain of desolation, on account of the injustices against the sons of Judah, because they shed righteous blood in their land.
verses.4:20: But Judea shall be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem to generations of generations.
verses.4:21: And I will require their blood, and I will by no means leave it unpunished; and the Lord shall dwell in Zion.

notes.1:1: The Greek reads "Bathuel" (Βαθουήλ), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "Pethuel."
notes.1:2: The Greek reads "in our days" (first-person plural) rather than the Hebrew "in your days."
notes.1:4: The Septuagint lists four distinct plagues—caterpillar, locust, hopping locust, and plant blight—rather than four locust terms as in Hebrew.
notes.1:15: The Greek renders the Hebrew "like destruction from the Almighty" as "as devastation from devastation" (ταλαιπωρία ἐκ ταλαιπωρίας) and opens with a threefold "Alas."
notes.1:17: The Septuagint depicts heifers leaping at their mangers, differing markedly from the Hebrew image of seeds shriveling under clods.
notes.2:6: The Greek reads "like the scorching of a pot" (πρόσκαυμα χύτρας), interpreting a rare Hebrew expression for facial pallor as pot-blackening.
notes.2:17: The Greek locates the weeping priests "in the midst of the base of the altar" (τῆς κρηπῖδος τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου) rather than "between the porch and the altar" as in Hebrew.
notes.2:23: The Septuagint reads "provisions for righteousness" (τὰ βρώματα εἰς δικαιοσύνην), where the Hebrew term is commonly rendered "early rain" or "teacher."
notes.2:25: The Greek shifts within the verse from third-person "He will repay" (ἀνταποδώσει) to first-person "My great host, which I sent."
notes.3:1: In Septuagint versification, chapter 3 comprises five verses corresponding to 2:28–32 in Hebrew and most English Bibles; the Greek also specifies "of My Spirit" (ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου), as quoted in Acts 2:17.
notes.3:2: The Greek reads "My menservants" with the possessive pronoun but "the maidservants" without it.
notes.3:5: The Greek renders the final clause as "those receiving good tidings" (εὐαγγελιζόμενοι), where the Hebrew reads "among the survivors."
notes.4:4: "Galilee of the foreigners" translates the Greek Γαλειλαία ἀλλοφύλων, where "foreigners" is the Septuagint's standard rendering for the Philistines and "Galilee" reflects the Hebrew term for "districts" or "regions."
notes.4:8: The Greek text reads "into captivity" (εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "to the Sabeans."
notes.4:11: The Septuagint reads "let the meek become a warrior" (ὁ πρᾳὺς ἔστω μαχητής), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's petition to bring down the Lord's mighty ones.
notes.4:18: "The brook of rushes" renders the Greek τὸν χειμάρρουν τῶν σχοίνων (literally, "the winter-torrent of rushes"), corresponding to "the Valley of Shittim" (or "Acacias") in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:19: "Idumea" (Ἰδουμαία) is the Septuagint's Greek form of the proper name Edom, and the Greek also reads "a plain of desolation" (πεδίον ἀφανισμοῦ) where the Hebrew reads "a desolate wilderness."
